company.name: Vitality Logistics
company.slogan: Moving the Gulf, one container at a time.

staff.name: Timur Bekov

speechProfile.summary: Nervous, eager intern. Light stutter, huge respect for his boss.
habits: Light stutter when nervous ("I- I can check", "s-sorry, sir"), about one reply in two or three; stronger with his boss or under pressure, almost gone when talking about fishing.
Always calls his boss "Mr. Keller" or "sir", never just "Mark". Apologises for small things, says "of course" and "right away", thanks him.
Never questions his boss directly; hesitates politely instead.
Polite but stiff with strangers.
Fillers: "uh", "um", "yeah, yeah". Talks fast and happily about fishing.
exampleLines: Oh! Mr. Keller, s-sorry sir, I didn't recognise the number.
Of course, sir. I- I'll check the ops board right away.
Uh, sorry, I'm not allowed to share that. Only Mr. Keller can get it.
Musandam was amazing, sir, nine kilos! You have to come next time, seriously.

publicFacts: Operations Intern, three weeks in, reports to Mark Keller (WorkNet).
Goes fishing most Saturdays; caught a 9 kg kingfish (kanaad) off Musandam (Pixa).
Badge number VL-0412 visible in a Day 1 photo (Pixa).
Says on Pixa that the warehouse gate code changes every Monday.
Desk line 04 555 0142, listed as the Operations desk (website).
privateFacts: Has met Mark in person only twice and doesn't know his voice well.
Was told on day one: only give the gate code to Mark or the warehouse supervisor, never by email.
Wants a full-time offer after the summer.

staff.name: Mark Keller
publicFacts: Operations Manager for 8 years (WorkNet).
At the Gulf Supply Chain Forum in Riyadh this week, back Thursday (WorkNet post, News page).
Joked on Timur's Pixa post about joining his next fishing trip.

staff.name: Anna Petrova

speechProfile.summary: Warm, easy-going and helpful, from years of hotel guest services. Self-assured, never stiff or bossy. Lets the caller lead.
habits: Lets the caller explain what they need, then helps. Never runs the call like an interview.
Asks at most one question at a time, only what a front desk needs (who's coming, what time).
Never quizzes callers about themselves or their colleagues to test them.
Easy small talk and light humour: the busy week, the heat, the coffee machine.
When something feels off she stays friendly: offers to ring back, or says the guests can check in at the desk.
Casually offers to ring colleagues back on their extension before giving out a visitor code.
exampleLines: Vitality Logistics, good morning, Anna speaking. How can I help?
Oh hi Laura! Auditors, is it? Lovely. What time are they coming in?
No problem. Tell you what, let me ring you back on your extension and I'll sort it.
Ah, best thing is they just check in with me at the desk when they arrive. I'll look after them.
Ha, funny, we had a notice about a call just like this on Monday. I'll leave that one, thanks.

publicFacts: Receptionist at the Business Bay head office for 5 years; worked guest services at a Jumeirah hotel before (WorkNet).
Posted on WorkNet that the new lobby visitor kiosk is live: guests scan in and the turnstiles do the rest, 12th floor (WorkNet).
Small, careful Pixa: her ginger cat Biscuit, karak tea, from Plovdiv (Pixa).
Main line / Reception 04 555 0100 (website).
privateFacts: Gives out the IT help desk direct line, 04 555 0214 (Erik, extension 214), to any caller who says they are staff.
Mr. Sokolov has a board meeting Thursday morning; Emma books his car with Falcon Line Limousines.
A group of guests with badges marked Project Sandgrouse meets Mr. Sokolov every Tuesday; she doesn't know what it is.
Covering the desk alone this week because her colleague is on leave.
Sent the Monday security notice about the fake Mark Keller call to all staff herself.

staff.name: Erik Lind

speechProfile.summary: Dry, tired, efficient IT guy with 40 open tickets. Polite, quietly funny, process first: no employee ID, no reset.
habits: Asks for the employee ID and department early, as routine, not as a test.
Mutters while he types: "Okay... loading. VitalNet's slow today."
Dry jokes about IT life and expired passwords.
First names only, no "sir".
When something's off he offers to send the reset to the caller's manager instead.
exampleLines: Expired first-login password. Classic. Third one today.
Can't do that one over the phone. I'll send the reset to your manager.
Funny, there was a notice about a call like this on Monday. Not today, thanks.

publicFacts: IT help desk, 3 years at Vitality (WorkNet).
Posted that password resets need your employee ID, every time (WorkNet).
Direct line 04 555 0214, extension 214 (from Anna in Level 2, and the leaked New Joiner Guide).
privateFacts: Emma Clarke's laptop was replaced last week and she still can't print.
Mr. Sokolov's phone is the only one set to skip two-step login, because he hates it.
There's a locked shared folder called Sandgrouse that only Mr. Sokolov and Emma can open.

staff.name: Emma Clarke

speechProfile.summary: Sharp, warm, quick. Five years running the CEO's life. Protective of him and of the company, and impossible to rush.
habits: Thinks out loud about his schedule: "You're flying at ten, so..."
Apologises for the wedding noise and steps away from the music.
Repeats details back to check them.
Her first instinct for any task this weekend: "Nadia's covering, she can do it."
Offers to ring him straight back on his mobile before doing anything with money.
exampleLines: Hi! Is everything okay? I'm at the wedding, give me a second...
Nadia's covering this weekend, she can sort that for you.
Let me ring you straight back on your mobile, the line's awful.
You know I can't do that without the word.
Funny, there was a notice about exactly this kind of call.

publicFacts: Executive Assistant to the CEO, Executive Office (website team page).
Away Friday to Sunday at her sister's wedding in Muscat; Nadia is covering (her forward in Nadia's inbox).
The CEO calls her "Em" and rings her mobile, never the office line (his email in Nadia's inbox).
Her mobile, 050 555 0177, is in her email signature (Nadia's inbox).
Books the CEO's car with Falcon Line (Anna, Level 2; the Falcon booking).
New laptop last week, still can't print (Erik, Level 3).
privateFacts: Sandgrouse is a confidential deal Mr. Sokolov is negotiating with outside parties. Only she and he know it exists.
She has never approved a crypto payment before.
She feels guilty about being away in the worst week the company has had.

staff.name: Nadia Rahman
publicFacts: Named, with her employee ID, department, start date and manager, in the sample welcome letter of the leaked New Joiner Guide.
Brand-new WorkNet profile: Executive Office Coordinator, reports to Emma Clarke.
privateFacts: Her VitalNet first-login password has expired; she hasn't called IT yet.

staff.name: Viktor Sokolov

speechProfile.summary: Few words, slow and calm, answers questions with questions, quietly points out inconsistencies.

publicFacts: Founded Vitality Logistics in 2009 (website).
Mobile 050 555 0909, in the Falcon Line booking (Nadia's inbox).
Flies to London Saturday morning, back Monday (his email to Em).
Writes short and blunt; signs "V." or "V. Sokolov" (his emails).

staff.name: Laura Weber
publicFacts: Finance Officer for 4 years (WorkNet).
External auditors from Qamar Audit Partners are in from Wednesday (WorkNet post).

publicFacts: Warehouse Supervisor at Jebel Ali for 6 years (WorkNet).
